definitions.gloss: easy to eat; palatable; not hard to chew or swallow
definitions.explanation: Describing food that is convenient, comfortable, or simple to consume, whether due to size, texture, flavor, or preparation.

examples.japanese: {一口|ひとくち}サイズで{食|た}べやすい。
examples.english: It's bite-sized and easy to eat.

examples.japanese: この{魚|さかな}は{骨|ほね}が{少|すく}なくて{食|た}べやすい。
examples.english: This fish has few bones and is easy to eat.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもでも{食|た}べやすいように、{小|ちい}さく{切|き}ってから{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I cut it into small pieces before serving so that even children could eat it easily.

notes:
Formed from the verb {食|た}べる (to eat) + やすい (easy to do). This is a productive grammatical pattern where verb stem + やすい creates an i-adjective meaning "easy to [verb]." The opposite pattern is verb stem + にくい (hard to do).

USAGE:
- Conjugates as a regular i-adjective: {食|た}べやすくない (not easy to eat), {食|た}べやすかった (was easy to eat)
- Can refer to size, texture, flavor mildness, or convenience of a food
- The ～やすい pattern is extremely productive: {読|よ}みやすい (easy to read), {使|つか}いやすい (easy to use), {分|わ}かりやすい (easy to understand)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {食|た}べやすい{大|おお}きさ: an easy-to-eat size
- {食|た}べやすい{味|あじ}: a mild, palatable flavor
- {食|た}べやすく{切|き}る: to cut into easy-to-eat pieces
- お{年寄|としよ}りにも{食|た}べやすい: easy to eat even for elderly people

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {食|た}べにくい: hard to eat — the opposite; food that is difficult to consume
- {口当|くちあ}たりがいい: pleasant to the palate — focuses on flavor and texture
- {手軽|てがる}に{食|た}べられる: can be eaten easily/casually — focuses on convenience
